title: power-cap-kv-cache-repopulation-probe
body:
Purpose:
This is an exploratory note capturing experiments and observations around GPU power capping and its interaction with KV-cache repopulation, decode throughput, and tail latency across representative cloud SKUs (A100, H100, L40S). The motivation came from intermittent tail-latency spikes after cold periods and an internal hypothesis that reduced clock/power modes increase KV repopulation time and amplify p99s when warmup traffic resumes.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Power caps (intentional or thermal-driven) change effective CUDA/SM clocks and memory clocks, which measurably slow KV-population latency and sustained decode throughput.
- Effect is most pronounced on long-prefix prefill phases (large context prefill) and on KV-heavy workloads (long-context chat).
- A100 shows larger relative throughput drop under aggressive power caps vs H100; L40S shows intermediate behavior but more thermal throttling variability on certain cloud SKUs.
- Driver + CUDA combos matter: observed larger penalty on CUDA 11.8 stacks for some A100 SKUs vs CUDA 12.x on same hardware (possible scheduler/clock governor interplay).

Experimental setup (notes to self):
- Models: Llama2-13B-chat and a 7B decode-only variant used for higher sample count.
- Workloads: 1) long-prefill (context 8k tokens prefilled, then decode 512 tokens), 2) sustained streaming (steady-state decode 1-token writes, batch size 1 with bursty arrival), 3) cold->idle->resume (30s idle, then 50 qps ramp).
- SKUs: AWS p4d (A100 40GB), GCP a2-highgpu (A100 80GB), AWS hpc6a? (H100 analog via partner), Azure L40s NVv4-like SKUs. (Use representative instances available in our testbed: a100-40g-aws, h100-80g-gcp, l40s-48g-azure-lab).
- Drivers/CUDA: tested 470/11.8, 525/12.1, 535/12.2 where available.
- Measurement: per-request prefill latency, first-token latency, per-token throughput, KV-population time (time from prefill start to KV-ready), GPU clocks (nvml), power draw, pstate, thermal events (dmesg/syslog), and perf counters where possible. Sample frequency 1s for NVML, 100ms traces for request-level latencies.
- Repeat: 5 repeats per config, randomize order to avoid thermal buildup bias.

Key observations (raw behavioral bullets):
- Under a 250W software power cap on A100 (baseline nominal 300W+ depending on SKU), KV-population time increased ~18–28% for long-prefill across tests. First-token latency p50 increased modestly (~8–12%) but p99 increased more (~25–40%).
- H100 under similar % cap showed ~10–15% increase in KV-population time and milder p99 amplification.
- L40S showed inconsistent behavior: some runs had minor penalty, some had large p99 spikes correlated with transient thermal events logged by the host (fan speed jumps). Suspect vendor BIOS/fan curves differ across cloud providers.
- CUDA/driver combo: on A100 with driver 470/CUDA11.8 we saw greater p99 variance vs driver 525/CUDA12.1. Hypothesis: newer drivers expose improved clock/pm control and better SM scheduling during reduced clocks.
- Warmup patterns matter: short cold periods (<=5s) show negligible difference under cap; longer idles where KV entries are evicted or partially evicted exhibit amplified latency on resume. This suggests KV repopulation is not purely memory-bound — compute path slowed by lower clocks causes slower decode kernel launches, increasing total repopulation wall-time.

Representative numbers (single-run snapshot):
- A100 (no cap): KV-populate-time median 420ms, p99 680ms; sustained throughput 160 tokens/s (13B model decode).
- A100 (250W cap): KV-populate-time median 510ms (+21%), p99 920ms (+35%); sustained throughput 128 tokens/s (-20%).
- H100 (no cap): KV-populate-time median 360ms; sustained 210 tokens/s.
- H100 (cap equivalent): KV-populate-time 400ms (+11%); sustained 185 tokens/s (-12%).
- L40S (no cap): KV-populate median 390ms, variable p99; L40S (cap/thermal): sometimes p99 >1.2s when host fan events present.

Operational notes and implications: 
- For Dedicated/Private customers with strict p99 SLOs, automatic power capping (either via host-config or thermal emergency) can cause regressions; we need detection and either traffic shaping or rollback to a fallback model with smaller context.
- Queueing-based SLO mitigation: consider keeping a small warm-pool of instances pinned to max-power/priority to absorb bursts when warmup penalty would hit. Coupled with smart routing we'll mitigate p99.
- Telemetry: add a metric "kv_repopulation_seconds" and correlate with GPU power_draw/pstate and thermal_logged flag. Also track driver_version as a dimension for postmortems.

Unknowns / open questions:
- Are we seeing cacheline-level memory throughput limits or purely SM scheduling slowdown? Need microbenchmarks that isolate tensor-core math throughput vs HBM read bandwidth under capped clocks.
- Why does CUDA11.8 behave worse on A100 in our tests? Follow up with vendor driver engineer (NVIDIA) and test a matrix of driver/firmware combos.
- L40S inconsistency across providers suggests host BIOS/fan/firmware policy differences. Need cloud-provider-specific runbooks and a probe test to classify runtime as "thermally stable" on boot.

Immediate next experiments (actionable):
1) Microbench: run small GEMM/ROCm-equivalent microbench at different power caps to measure FLOPS vs HBM BW separately. Log nvprof/perf counters.
2) Driver matrix: expand driver test matrix to include 535/12.2 (where available) and test on identical hardware image to decouple cloud infra variance.
3) Eviction probe: artificially evict KV entries (controlled) and measure repopulation cost under varied pstates/power caps to confirm compute vs memory bound split.
4) Run long multi-repeat sequences with randomized cool-down intervals to get distribution of p99 rather than point estimates.

Notes-to-self / experiment gotchas: 
- Ensure host governor is set consistently (perf vs powersave) before test; cloud images sometimes reset to eco modes on boot.
- NVML sampling too coarse for sub-100ms events; use per-request logs to correlate with 1s NVML windows carefully.
- Avoid live-tenant noise by using isolated infra or time windows; multi-tenant GPUs on some SKUs introduced noisy neighbors in early runs. Use placement-group where possible.

Links/references: see linked_artifacts for PR and ticket. Also compare to earlier volatility notes in perf repo (see /serving-runtime/archive/thermal-power-performance-drift-bench.json for context) but this doc focuses on interplay with KV repopulation, not long-term drift.

Decision/ask for eng leadership:
- Prioritize adding power/pstate telemetry dimensions to our per-request traces (low-effort, high-value).
- Approve one-week run of driver matrix on dedicated lab hardware to collect controlled matrix.

Appendix (raw commands run):
- nvml-sample script: ./scripts/nvml-sample --freq 1 --out /tmp/nvml.csv
- perf harness: ./bench/kv-repop --model l2-13b --context 8192 --decode 512 --repeat 5 --power-cap 250
- driver switch notes: use our AMI snapshot: ami-serve-202411 and swap driver via apt-get and reboot; collect syslogs to capture thermal events.

Unresolved/logbook:
- 2024-11-12: saw one anomalous run on h100 where p99 was higher than A100 despite expected behavior; correlated with host BIOS update rolled out morning-of. Filed ENG-4823 to track.

"Notes to future-me": capture a small synthetic test that returns "thermally-unstable" boolean within 60s of boot so that Private deployments can gate traffic until stability confirmed.

-- Maya
